label: Actor-level colour/pictorial jurisdiction in Schlözer: fact versus relation/display

observations.value: Schlözer rejects colouring Facta in 1772, defends painted chronological co-presence as a mnemonic for Synchronismus in 1773, and is secondarily reported in 1775 to propose table illumination for period duration. The legitimacy of visual/chromatic intervention is therefore layer-specific rather than governed by a general pro-/anti-colour stance.

Colour can be treated as an actor-grounded test of epistemic jurisdiction: what operation colour or pictorialization is allowed to perform, at which point in historical knowledge production, and under what warrant.

claim_limit: This does not establish that the Gatterer-Schlözer Species Facti polemic explicitly debated colour. The 1773 positive control belongs to the Herder controversy.

label: Directly close Schlözer's fact-versus-display colour/pictorial jurisdiction
notes: 1772 directly establishes the negative fact-layer boundary. The 1773 part-II work and p.327 locus are bibliographically fixed for the positive painted-synchronism passage, but exact wording still needs direct page inspection. A separate 1775 secondary quotation reports Illumination der Tabelle for period duration and still lacks a primary page locator.
reopen_rule: Inspect ULB Sachsen-Anhalt DOI 10.25673/95815 p.327; then search DOI 10.25673/95805 for Illumination der Tabelle. Keep the 1773 Herder controversy separate from the Gatterer Species Facti quarrel.

label: Gatterer human colour classification: proposal, causal testing and demotion, 1771–1789
notes: Araújo 2012 supplies a much sharper trajectory. Gatterer's 1771 Einleitung, pp. 61-62, treats outward human differences as zufällige rather than wesentliche Unterscheidungszeichen/Varietäten. His 1775 Abriß der Geographie, pp. 4-5, nevertheless projects an Anthropographie/Geographie der Menschenkörper using Gestalt and Hautfarben as classificatory categories. By the 1789 Kurzer Begriff der Geographie, vol. 2, p. 606, language is preferred over skin colour as a solid proof of peoples' origin; colour survives as a fallback where reliable linguistic information is missing. Araújo concludes that Gatterer renounced accidental bodily colour as an organisatorisches Prinzip of geography/history.
reopen_rule: Directly inspect Gatterer 1771 pp. 61-62, 1775 pp. 3-5 and 1789 vol.2 p.606. Encode the exact shift from visible bodily difference to candidate classifier to epistemically demoted fallback. Distinguish observability from classificatory and causal/genealogical warrant.

label: Gatterer demotes skin colour from proposed human-geographical classifier to a weaker fallback criterion
subject: agent.johann-christoph-gatterer
object: Hautfarbe as a criterion for classifying peoples

sources.citation: André de Melo Araújo, Weltgeschichte in Göttingen (Bielefeld: transcript, 2012), pp. 141-145, 153, 178
Johann Christoph Gatterer, Abriß der Geographie (Göttingen: Dieterich, 1775), pp. 3-5
Johann Christoph Gatterer, Kurzer Begriff der Geographie, vol. 2 (Göttingen: Dieterich, 1789), p. 606
Johann Christoph Gatterer, Einleitung in die synchronische Universalhistorie (Göttingen: Vandenhoeck, 1771), pp. 61-62

observations.value: Gestalt and Hautfarben projected for Anthropographie/Geographie der Menschenkörper as differentiating/classificatory criteria
Outward bodily differences are treated as accidental varieties rather than essential differences
Language is preferred as stronger evidence of peoples' origin; skin colour functions only where better linguistic evidence is unavailable
A perceptually obvious colour difference can fail as an organising principle because visibility does not supply sufficient genealogical/causal warrant.

claim_limit: Keep secondary_scholarship/probable until the three primary loci are directly inspected. Do not redescribe this as a modern racial taxonomy without primary contextual control.

label: Gatterer supplies an actor-grounded negative control for colour at the classification layer

observations.value: Literal bodily colour can be empirically visible and initially proposed as a classifier, yet be demoted because it does not provide the required causal/genealogical warrant for historical-geographical organisation.
The colour-method ontology must distinguish perceptual discriminability from classificatory warrant and from causal/essential warrant.

claim_limit: This is a strong secondary reconstruction, not yet a primary-direct actor statement of a unified colour methodology.
